# 7490 - Decade counter

Package DIP-14 · family 74 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/7490.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/7490.json)

## Symbol

| As printed in ND-13.003.01, page 20 | Drawn in ND style | Drawn in modern style |
|---|---|---|
| ![7490 as printed in the 1976 symbol manual](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/7490.png) | ![7490 drawn in nd style](../../../catalog/symbols/nd1976/shapes/block-7490.png) | ![7490 drawn in modern style](../../../catalog/symbols/modern/shapes/block-7490.png) |

A rectangle for the whole function (or one section of it). Pin numbers are written on the lines where they meet the box; signal names are written beside them.

How to tell it on a drawing: Read the part type from the parts list and compare the pin numbers against this cut-out.

All symbols: [symbol catalogue](../../SYMBOL-CATALOG.md).

## Functions

| Output pin | Formula | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | QA = stateA | Divide-by-two stage, clocked by input A. |
| 9 | QB = stateB | Bit B of the second section, clocked by input B. |
| 8 | QC = stateC | Bit C of the second section. |
| 11 | QD = stateD | Bit D of the second section. |

## Stored state

Bits stored: 4

Changes on: falling edge of A (QA) and of B (QB, QC, QD)

- R0(1) and R0(2) both high, and R9(1) or R9(2) low: QD QC QB QA = 0000 at once
- R9(1) and R9(2) both high: QD QC QB QA = 1001 at once (takes priority over R0)
- Otherwise (at least one R0 low and at least one R9 low): count
- QA toggles on each falling edge of A
- QD QC QB count 0,1,2,3,4 (divide by five) on falling edges of B
- With QA connected to B and pulses on A: QD QC QB QA count BCD 0-9
- With QD connected to A and pulses on B: bi-quinary count, QA gives a divide-by-ten square wave

## Notes

Edge: the block diagram draws master-slave flip-flops with an inverted clock on A and B; the outputs change on the high-to-low transition. QA is tested at IOL 16 mA plus the B-input load, so QA can drive B and still keep full fan-out. The datasheet gives no minimum propagation delays; the path-delay function uses 0 ns for the minimum.
